messages:
customer-sre: FYI - customer 'acme' is hitting intermittent TLS handshake failures + 502s when calling our hosted API via their TGW->spoke->VPC endpoint. From EC2 inside the spoke no issue. From on-prem (DX) it fails. Seen since yesterday afternoon, high impact. Can someone take?

support_jess: sorry for the trouble - can you paste a quick repro (dig + curl -v) from both an EC2 in the spoke and from their on-prem box? Also which endpoint type (Interface) and did they enable Private DNS? @eng-marta fyi in case routing/kernel tweaks matter.

customer-sre: grabbing outputs. note they use a Transit Gateway attachment (shared account). Endpoint is an Interface endpoint in our account, service name is com.amazonaws.vpce.us-west-2.vpce-svc-0abcd1234 (cross-account). Private DNS was not explicitly enabled by them when they created it.

acme-netops: here's the on-prem trace and dig/curl we ran (sanitized):
```
# dig from on-prem using their resolver
$ dig +short api.redwood.example.com @10.2.4.5
52.45.123.210

# curl from on-prem
$ curl -vk https://api.redwood.example.com/health
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood.example.com/health
* Trying 52.45.123.210...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to 52.45.123.210 (52.45.123.210) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering h2
* TLS handshake has read 0 bytes and written 300 bytes
* SSL connection using TLSv1.2 / ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
* Server certificate:
*  subject: CN=internal-nlb-123456.elb.amazonaws.com
*  start date: Jan  1 00:00:00 2025 GMT
*  expire date: Jan  1 23:59:59 2026 GMT
*  subjectAltName: host "api.redwood.example.com" matched cert's "internal-nlb-123456.elb.amazonaws.com"? no.
* SSL: certificate subject name (internal-nlb-123456.elb.amazonaws.com) does not match target host name 'api.redwood.example.com'
* Closing connection 0
curl: (51) SSL: certificate subject name (internal-nlb-123456.elb.amazonaws.com) does not match target host name 'api.redwood.example.com'
```

customer-sre: and from an EC2 in the spoke (same VPC/subnet as the endpoint ENIs):
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.example.com @172.31.0.2
10.0.5.12

$ curl -vk https://api.redwood.example.com/health
* Connected to 10.0.5.12 (10.0.5.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake completed successfully
* Server certificate: CN=api.redwood.example.com
* HTTP/2 200
{"status":"ok"}
```

support_jess: interesting - on-prem resolves to a public IP (52.45.x.x) while EC2 resolves to a private ENI IP. That smells like Private DNS / split-horizon. Two quick checks: 1) is Private DNS enabled on the interface endpoint? 2) do they have a Route53 private hosted zone that overrides the name? also is there a Resolver inbound endpoint or forwarder for on-prem DNS?

acme-netops: we do have a private hosted zone for api.redwood.example.com in our account but it points to the public NLB A record (we were trying to pin to the public NLB previously). We also use a Route53 resolver endpoint for inbound queries from on-prem -> AWS. Private hosted zone exists in the spoke account.

eng-marta: thanks, this matches the symptom. TL;DR: on-prem DNS -> Resolver inbound -> resolves the name using the spoke account private zone which currently points at the public NLB IP; EC2 uses VPC resolver and gets the ENI via interface endpoint/Private DNS. So return path differs and cert mismatch occurs. Two remediation paths: enable Private DNS on the VPC Endpoint OR update the private hosted zone to point at the interface endpoint IPs (but that is brittle since endpoints have ENIs per AZ). Preferred: enable Private DNS so Route53 automatically maps the service name to the endpoint's private IPs for VPCs that use that endpoint. Also consider removing the legacy private hosted zone record.

support_jess: other quick items to validate: security group on endpoint allows inbound from the spoke and TGW attachment, and the endpoint policy doesn't block traffic. Also confirm that TGW route tables don't send reply traffic back out the wrong attachment (looping).

infra-bot: endpoint-checker: VPC Endpoint vpce-03b2... exists in us-west-2, PrivateDnsEnabled=false, interface ENIs: [10.0.5.12, 10.1.2.14], owner account: redwood-account, ServiceName: com.amazonaws.vpce.us-west-2.vpce-svc-0abcd1234

customer-sre: confirmed - Private DNS disabled. We didn't realize cross-account endpoints need owner to enable Private DNS or the customer to re-create with it on.

eng-marta: cross-account note: Private DNS can be enabled by the endpoint owner only. We created the endpoint on behalf of the customer in our account but left Private DNS off due to initial testing. Quick fix options: 1) we (Redwood) enable Private DNS on the endpoint (preferred) so their Resolver and VPCs see private mapping; 2) they update their private hosted zone to alias the name to the interface endpoint ENIs (not recommended). Also they could keep current setup but then their DNS resolver graph has to resolve to the private ENIs from on-prem (inbound resolver + conditional forwarding to our VPC), but that's more complex.

support_jess: from a repro point of view, after enabling Private DNS, please re-run dig from on-prem (via resolver) and ensure it returns 10.0.5.12 not the public 52.45.x.x. Once that returns private IP and curl -vk succeeds with cert CN=api.redwood.example.com we should be green.

acme-netops: ok please enable Private DNS - we'll stand by and re-test.

infra-bot: action_log: Modified VPC Endpoint vpce-03b2... - set PrivateDnsEnabled=true by operator support_jess at 2025-08-15T18:02:34Z

customer-sre: re-testing now...
```
# dig via their on-prem -> resolver
$ dig +short api.redwood.example.com @10.2.4.5
10.0.5.12

# curl
$ curl -vk https://api.redwood.example.com/health
* Connected to 10.0.5.12 (10.0.5.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake completed successfully
* Server certificate: CN=api.redwood.example.com
* HTTP/2 200
{"status":"ok"}
```

support_jess: nice - looks fixed. leaving note: we also removed the legacy A record in their private hosted zone to avoid future confusion.

eng-marta: follow-ups: 1) for cross-account TGW scenarios document in KB: need to ensure Private DNS for interface endpoints or ensure resolver rules/hosted zones point to endpoint addresses. 2) validate endpoint policy + SG as part of onboarding checklist. I'll open a doc PR.

customer-sre: customer confirmed no more errors. Closing incident. :tada:
